paper_id: Ma et al. - 2015 - Opportunistic Concurrency A MAC Protocol for Wireless Sensor Networks
title: Opportunistic Concurrency: A MAC Protocol for Wireless Sensor Networks
motivation: CSMA deferring transmissions on busy channels wastes opportunities when physical layer could decode concurrent signals.
problem_framing: How to enable distributed nodes to exploit capture-effect/MIM for parallel transmission instead of serial waiting.
key_insight: Local SINR map allows each node to independently decide if concurrent transmission will succeed without disturbing ongoing links.
method_signature: Concurrency map + SINR-based decision + embedded X-MAC
evaluation_criteria: Latency (17% reduction), throughput (9.4% gain), energy (10% reduction) in 60-node testbed.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: When Cmax is 3 or 4, collision increases. More concurrency suffers from hidden-terminal asymmetry.
evidence_for_taste: more concurrent transmissions, thus increases the performance
we didn’t allow any transmission decision that will result in any other transmission failure
thinking_moves: Identify concrete deferral opportunities via validation experiment on CC2420
Distill lightweight distributed decision mechanism from physical-layer capability
Embed as modular assistant component rather than replacing existing MAC
Map spatial distribution of concurrency gains across topology
Observe multi-hop packets benefit incrementally at each hop
cites_own_work: Walking down the Stairs collision resolution
